title: A Parish for the Witness
premise: When estate lawyer Casper Vasquez is called to probate a will naming the town's founder as its testator—signed eleven years after his burial—the empty coffin unearthed from the churchyard confirms something impossible is happening in the coastal parish of Merrow's End. Casper, who has spent a decade filing away the town's secrets after fleeing their own past identity, must trace the will to a witness everyone insists died in the flood of 2014. The search unravels the found family that took Casper in, revealing that the founder faked his death to protect the witness—Casper's own estranged mother—and that the tide has been holding the truth offshore all along. In the end, Casper chooses to file nothing away: they testify openly, inherit not money but a family rebuilt on honesty, and watch the sea finally give back what it took.
about_author: Silas Dunmore is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent seven years cataloguing wills, deeds, and unclaimed coffins in small coastal towns before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about the paperwork people leave behind when they try to disappear.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. A courier delivers a probate petition for Edmund Harrow, founder of Merrow's End, dead and buried since 2014. The signature is dated three years ago. Casper, whose whole life is orderly files, feels the first crack in their alphabetized calm. Emotional beat: dread disguised as professional curiosity.

chapters.title: Exhumation at Low Tide
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. The court orders exhumation; half the town gathers on the bluff to watch. The coffin comes up light, and inside: sand, a folded coat, and no body. Sheriff Ida Brandt fixes Casper with a look that says you knew him best. Emotional beat: communal shock curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Alphabetized Secrets
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Flashbacks braid with present as Casper rereads their own case files, realizing how many clients paid them to look away—including a woman calling herself 'M. Reyes' who signed papers in 2015. Emotional beat: guilt surfacing; Casper admits their tidy career was built on not asking questions.

chapters.title: The Witness Everyone Buried
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Casper and Sheriff Brandt. The will requires a living witness: 'R. Vasquez.' Casper's own surname—and their mother Ruth, officially drowned in the 2014 flood. Brandt reveals she's been sitting on an anonymous letter postmarked last month. Emotional beat: vertigo; the mystery turns inward.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. At the flood memorial, townsfolk share contradictory memories of Ruth Vasquez—saint, swindler, ghost. Casper's found family, the Okafor sisters who raised them after the flood, beg them to stop digging. Emotional beat: loyalty versus truth; the first real fracture in Casper's chosen family.

chapters.title: A Coffin Full of Sand
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Forensics on the grave sand shows it came from a specific cove—Gullwrack Cove, where the Okafors keep their oyster lease. Someone used the family's boat ramp the night of the 'burial.' Emotional beat: betrayal sharpening into resolve; Casper can no longer protect anyone by staying quiet.

chapters.title: The Second Funeral
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Digging through Harrow's sealed estate, Casper finds a second, older will leaving everything to Ruth—dated two weeks before the flood. Harrow didn't die in 2014; he was helped out of town, and Ruth helped him. Emotional beat: grief reframed—Casper's mother may be alive, and complicit.

chapters.title: Storm Glass
chapters.summary: POV: Casper and Brandt. A nor'easter traps the town; someone burns the county archive annex, destroying the flood records. Casper realizes the arsonist is protecting Ruth—or hunting her. Brandt confesses she's known about the empty grave for a year and said nothing. Emotional beat: paranoia at full pitch; allies revealed as keepers of secrets too.

chapters.title: The Witness at Gullwrack
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Following the tide chart in Harrow's second will, Casper reaches Gullwrack Cove at spring low water and finds a live-aboard trawler—and Ruth Vasquez, alive, guarding the final secret: Harrow died for real two years ago, and she buried him herself to escape the men he owed. Emotional beat: reunion laced with fury; the climax of identity—mother and child, strangers.

chapters.title: A Parish for the Witness
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Back in open probate, Casper does what ten years of filing taught them never to do: tells the whole truth on the record. The town convulses, then chooses grace—the Okafors stand beside them, Brandt resigns honorably, and Ruth, spared prosecution as a cooperating witness, asks for nothing but a seat at Sunday dinner. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined—not property but belonging, earned by testimony.
